name: fig_access_bound.png
caption: Access to the source text bounds what a strategy can convey. (a) Hidden-full-text experiment: OMIM facts conveyed by direct reading on the same 46 entries, 136 curator paragraphs and 2,120 fixed facts when the papers readable in full were supplied as abstract only, as abstract plus second-hand passages from later open-access papers, or in full; means over entries. The full-text draft is scored before the repair round, so no arm is repaired. Paired differences from abstract only (bootstrap 95% intervals over entries): second-hand passages +4.9 points (+2.8 to +7.1; 33 entries better, 9 worse, 4 tied); full text +43.7 points (+38.3 to +49.1; 45 better, 0 worse, 1 tied). (b) Whether the text supplied for a paper states each of the 6,239 fixed facts of the 93 compared entries, by how the paper was readable, as percentages of each row pooled over facts: stated 1,246 of 1,639 facts about full-text papers, 1,099 of 4,221 about abstract-only papers and 27 of 379 about title-only papers; not stated 140, 2,239 and 290. (c) OMIM facts conveyed by each strategy on the facts the supplied text states (filled markers, 89 entries) and does not state (hollow markers, 90 entries); means over entries. The read-and-write and extract-then-write strategies convey 91.0 to 94.4% of stated facts and 5.5 to 6.9% of facts not stated, no more than the memory-only control on facts not stated (8.2%; control minus direct reading +1.3 points, 95% interval -1.4 to +4.6). Whether a fact is stated is a model judgement with verified quotes, not checked by a curator, and the same model family judged what the drafts convey.

name: fig_audit_coverage.png
caption: Share of planted errors that the claim-level audit flagged, one row per class (the dropped-qualifier class split by deletion rule), with flagged/total counts at right, over items whose truth is known by construction. An item counts as flagged when a planted claim was judged unsupported or contradicted (for omitted findings and the controls, when any claim in the paragraph was). Classes have 30 items each (26 and 25 truth-known for the same-entry swap and the moved sentence), each qualifier rule 2 to 8 (11 of 30 flagged in all), and the single-value row is the earlier test on 60 paragraphs; all were planted in evidence-graph paragraphs the audit had passed. Swapped citations, moved sentences, altered values and deleted negations (which reverse the claim) were all caught; deleted hedges and counts rarely, deleted zygosity or 'one family or patient' never. An added irrelevant citation and an omitted finding are invisible by design: a claim takes the best verdict over its cited papers, and the audit judges only what is written. Re-audited unaltered with fresh calls, no control paragraph was flagged (0 of 60, 0 of 113); these had passed the audit once, so this is not a false-flag rate on arbitrary paragraphs. The swaps are easy cases (the swapped paper is usually about something else), some qualifier deletions are nearly meaning-preserving, and the samples are small, so the figure shows direction and large effects, not a sensitivity estimate.

name: fig_design_vs_reading.png
caption: Paired differences in OMIM facts conveyed (percentage points; mean over entries with 95% bootstrap interval over entries), on all facts and on facts the supplied text states (papers readable in full; papers readable as abstract only) or does not state; whether the text states a fact is a model judgement, not checked by a curator. All panels share one scale but not one range. (a) Agentic curator, evidence graph and case table first minus direct reading, all after the repair round, on the 93 entries of the main comparison. (b) A separate comparison with its own baseline and entries: ways of reading better minus direct reading's draft before repair (no arm repaired), on held-out entries with at least one paper readable in full (38 entries; 35 for checklist plus completeness pass). Each panel averages over the entries with facts of its kind (a: 93, 40, 79, 90; b: 38, 34, 31, 36, or 35, 32, 28, 33 for the combined arm). Memory only and recall, then verify are omitted: on all facts and stated facts they lie 34.0 to 77.6 points below direct reading; on facts not stated, memory only is +1.3 (-1.4 to +4.6) and recall, then verify -4.8 (-6.7 to -3.0). Case table first falls behind on all facts (-1.9, -3.1 to -0.7) and most on stated facts in full-text papers (-8.4, -14.3 to -3.8); no interval of the evidence graph or the agentic curator excludes zero (the curator's on all facts ends at +0.0). The completeness pass, alone or after the checklist, gains most on stated facts in full-text papers (+4.5, +2.9 to +6.3; +6.3, +4.0 to +8.7), and its intervals on facts the text does not state include zero; the checklist's gain is small (+1.6, +0.5 to +2.7; sign test not below 0.05 after Holm adjustment), and the three-draft merge also gains on facts the text does not state (+1.5, +0.4 to +2.7).

name: fig_memory_by_era.png
caption: OMIM facts conveyed (top; primary endpoint) and causal gene F1 (bottom) for the memory-only control (black squares) and direct reading (blue circles), as means over entries by creation era (MIM-number range of the entry; n = compared entries per band). Hollow markers at right are a separate set of entries created in 2026, chosen by creation date alone and not used in developing the strategies; 20 of the 30 run are compared, since an entry counts only if every strategy completed it and stopped replies were frequent there. The memory-only control conveys 24.1% of facts for the 600000–609999 band but 5.7% for 620000 onward and 7.0% for the 2026 set (causal gene F1 41.2% and 30.0%), whereas direct reading conveys 51.2–53.9% from the 600000 band on (52.2% for the 2026 set) and reaches 100.0% gene F1 everywhere except the classic band (87.0%). The model's training cut-off is not known, so this is a contamination check, not proof that the reading results are free of memorisation: from the 600000 band on, direct reading's coverage of facts from abstract-only papers also declines with creation era (49.8% to 37.9%, pooled over facts).

name: fig_missed_facts.png
caption: Where the fixed OMIM facts that direct reading did not fully convey went, by how each cited paper could be read (pooled over facts; 97 entries with a draft, 466 OMIM paragraphs). Bars give each access level's facts as shares and are labelled with fact counts. Each missed fact was checked once against the text available for its paper and judged stated (with a quote verified in that text), partly stated, or not stated; this is a model judgement, not a curator's. Facts the draft conveyed only partly count as missed, and the small remainder of the full-text and abstract-only bars (7 and 25 facts) were contradicted by the draft. The right-hand column gives the share of missed facts that the available text states: 49% (245 of 501) for full-text papers, against 2% for abstract-only and 0% for title-only papers, where nearly all missed facts were only partly stated or not stated in the text the model had.

name: fig_overview.png
caption: Benchmark overview. Every strategy receives the same input for an entry e = (h, R): its header and exactly the papers the curators cited, each readable as full text, abstract or title only depending on open access; the causal gene is withheld. One model writes every draft and only the generation strategy varies: three paradigms, a memory-only control with no papers, add-ons (dashed) each tested against its parent, and four ways of reading better, variants of direct reading evaluated on held-out entries with at least one paper readable in full. The same guards apply to every strategy. The audit judges each atomic claim against the papers it cites (all verdicts are model judgements); flagged claims get one repair round, except in the memory-only control and the reading-better arms (the latter audited without repair on 20 of their 41 entries). Scoring uses curator-written text about the cited papers, not whole entries: each curator paragraph is split once into a fixed fact list, and OMIM facts conveyed, the primary endpoint, is the share of those facts present in what the draft says about the paper, with partly present facts counted as half. Whether the supplied text states a fact is a stored model judgement, identical for every strategy. Main set: 100 entries; 515 cited papers (96 full text, 345 abstract only, 74 title only); 476 curator paragraphs; 6,652 fixed facts.
